TopSource: https://success.vanillaforums.com/kb/articles/1842-api-v2-endpoints (embedded OpenAPI v3 spec, merged with the live open.vanillaforums.com endpoint)
ProceedReason: A real, machine-readable OpenAPI v3 contract was recovered from TWO independent live/embedded public Vanilla-hosted communities (open.vanillaforums.com's unauthenticated live endpoint + success.vanillaforums.com's KB-embedded snapshot) and merged into a single union spec: 335 paths, 380 component schemas, 79 independently-addressable REST resources ('doors'), of which 51 are COVERABLE record types with real numeric <object>ID PKs, real scalar FK fields, real PageNumber+Link-header pagination, and (for most objects) real Create/Update/Delete paths+methods. This clears the >=0.7 real-OpenAPI-coverage bar the workflow uses to decide whether to raise extraction's K value.

Sources.AccessNotes: Live, UNAUTHENTICATED GET returns the full OpenAPI v3.0.3 JSON directly (HTTP 200, no permission gate) -- verified fresh via curl (not WebFetch; a 1.6MB JSON schema must be fetched raw in code per the acquire-the-schema-raw discipline, WebFetch would summarize/truncate it). 237 paths, 290 component schemas, servers=[https://open.vanillaforums.com/api/v2]. This is the developer/open-source-flavored public Vanilla community (open.vanillaforums.com) with a narrower addon set enabled than the Success Community (no Knowledge Base/Articles/Analytics-dashboard addons on this instance), but it uniquely carries appeals, authenticator-types, ai-processing-preferences, data-sources, discussions/poll paths not present in the Success Community's snapshot. Saved raw to sources/vanilla-openapi.open-vanillaforums.v3.json.

The KB article's own React-hydration HTML payload embeds the COMPLETE OpenAPI v3 spec for the Success Community's own live instance (success.vanillaforums.com is itself a Vanilla-powered community, so its Dashboard > Settings > API Integrations > API V2 Swagger is baked into this public KB page as a 'specJson' data island -- the SpectaQL-style whole-schema-embedded-in-HTML pattern). openapi 3.0.2, info.version '2.0-alpha', servers=[https://success.vanillaforums.com/api/v2]. 316 paths, 350 component schemas -- richer than the open.vanillaforums.com instance because this community has the Knowledge Base/Articles, Analytics dashboards, and AI-settings addons enabled. IMPORTANT: the LIVE raw endpoint (https://success.vanillaforums.com/api/v2/openapi/v3) now returns HTTP 403 'Garden.Settings.Manage' for anonymous requests -- confirmed via direct curl, both with and without the historical '?disabled=true' query param seen in the KB page's own displayed example URL. The spec is therefore recovered from the PUBLIC KB page's embedded HTML payload, not the raw endpoint. Extraction method: curl -> save whole 18MB HTML -> Node script (packages/Integration/connectors-registry/higherlogic-vanilla/scripts, ad hoc) that HTML-entity-decodes + JSON-string-unescapes the 'specJson' field (11 embedded copies found at different escape depths on the page; only the most-deeply-escaped copy round-trips cleanly through JSON.parse -- the other 10 are the same payload, not distinct content, confirmed by comparing lengths). WebFetch on this URL returned ONLY the page <title> (SPA hydration payload not surfaced by WebFetch's HTML-to-markdown conversion) and a direct curl of the raw endpoint hit WebFetch's 10MB cap -- both are exactly the 'WebFetch is a summarizer, never source of record' failure mode this discipline warns about; the raw bytes were pulled via Bash/curl and parsed in code instead. Saved raw extracted spec to sources/vanilla-openapi.success-kb-embedded.v3.json.

WebFetch returned only the page title (same SPA-hydration issue as article 1842). Body text recovered via curl + a targeted Node extraction of the article's own 'body' JSON field (disambiguated from unrelated embedded-discussion-widget 'body' fields on the same page by anchoring on the exact article name in the surrounding JSON). Confirms: numbered pagination (page+limit params, first/last/prev/next) and 'more' pagination (first/prev/next only, used where totals would be expensive); paging info delivered via the Link response header (RFC 5988 style, rel=first/last/prev/next); a 'Paging-Next' header is always present when more rows exist; a 'fields' query param usable on every GET to select a sparse fieldset (also usable on CSV export). Extracted text saved to sources/kb-40-api-v2-overview.extracted.txt.

WebFetch returned only the page title; body recovered the same targeted-extraction way as article 40 (a plain, non-HTML-entity-encoded 'body' field was found this time -- the encoding style differs per KB render pass, so extraction script tries both the HTML-entity-encoded and the plain-JSON-string forms). Confirms explicit rate limits: GET requests limited to 300 requests / 1 minute / per IP; POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE limited to 120 requests / 1 minute / per IP; exceeding either returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, auto-lifting after 1 minute; a hard limit of >250 requests within 10 seconds can trigger a longer IP block requiring manual Vanilla Support intervention to lift. Feeds Integration.BatchMaxRequestCount / BatchRequestWaitTime. Extracted text saved to sources/kb-44-rate-limits.extracted.txt.

WebFetch returned only the page title; body recovered via the same targeted-extraction technique. Confirms: bearer-token auth via 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' header (preferred -- avoids header/token leakage into server logs) OR an 'access_token' query-string parameter (documented fallback for clients that cannot set custom headers / want to avoid CORS preflight); personal access tokens are generated per-user from the user's own profile (MeBox > Edit Profile > Access Tokens > Generate New Token), gated by the 'Garden > Tokens > Add' permission on the generating user's Role, and API calls made with the token carry that user's own permissions (not a separate service-account scope). Extracted text saved to sources/kb-41-personal-access-tokens.extracted.txt.
